title: AI video generation, on published capability and stated policy

subject.question: Which AI video generation product fits a team that needs an API, commercial rights, and a clear position on customer data?
subject.decision: picking a vendor to build a product on
subject.context: A DATED SNAPSHOT, retrieved 2026-08-26, of what each vendor's own documentation said on that day. This market changes monthly; treat every cell as of that date and re-check before relying on one. Every criterion is factual — a published capability or a stated policy — and no cell carries a quality judgement about any company. Where a cell is blank it is because the vendor's material did not settle it, and the blank says which kind. Each filled cell quotes the vendor's own words; the quotes were verified against the cited pages by a second pass, which corrected four of them.
ambiguities: "The product" is ambiguous where a vendor ships several models under one name — Sora 2 and sora-2-pro differ on resolution, and the figure recorded depends on which one you mean.
"Trains on customer content" is recorded per the tier the product is actually sold on, which is not always the tier the terms lead with.

groups.label: Published capability
groups.description: What the vendor says the model can do.

groups.label: Stated policy
groups.description: What the vendor's terms and policies say. Read from terms pages, never from marketing.

alternatives.label: Luma Ray3.2
alternatives.description: Recorded as Ray3.2 rather than Dream Machine: the vendor describes Ray3.2 as the current product, and every figure below comes from its documentation.

alternatives.label: OpenAI Sora 2
alternatives.description: The vendor announced removal of the Videos API and the sora-2 model aliases from the API on 2026-09-24, three weeks after this snapshot.

definition.question: The longest single generation the vendor publishes, in seconds, for the model named.
The vendor's highest published output resolution, expressed as pixel height so it is orderable. 720p = 720, 1080p = 1080, 4K = 2160.
Whether the product accepts a still image as the first frame.
Whether the model generates synchronised audio as part of the video, as distinct from a separate soundtrack or voiceover feature.
Whether a publicly documented API exists that anyone can sign up for.
Whether the terms expressly grant commercial use of outputs. Read from terms or licensing pages only, never from marketing copy.
Whether the vendor publicly states what the model was trained on with any specificity — a dataset, a corpus, a licensor. Naming modalities is not a disclosure of sources.

criteria.label: States that it trains on customer content

definition.question: Whether the vendor states that customer uploads and prompts ARE used to train its models. The value carries the direction: false means the vendor states it does not. It does not mean the vendor is silent — that would be a blank.

missingCodes.means: The vendor addresses the question and explicitly declines to answer it.

procedures.describedAs: one documentation pass per product, then a second pass that re-fetched every cited page and re-checked every quote character by character

comments.body: The first pass filled this for one vendor and blanked it for another on strictly more specific wording — the weaker disclosure got the stronger verdict. Both are blank now. Neither names a dataset, a corpus or a licensor, and a criterion applied unevenly between named competitors is worse than one nobody filled in.

Only one false here rests on a vendor actually denying it. The other blanks are absence-of-a-parameter, which is inference from silence — and one vendor generates audio with no audio parameter at all. Worth settling what evidence a false requires before this column is used.

missing.note: No Google terms page found that explicitly grants commercial use of Veo outputs. The Gemini API Additional Terms (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms) only disclaim ownership — "Google won't claim ownership over that content" — which is not the same as an express commercial-use grant. The Generative AI Additional Terms (https://policies.google.com/terms/generative-ai) are silent on both ownership and commercial use, deferring to the general Google Terms of Service. The Google Workspace Service Specific Terms do address Generated Output ownership, but govern Workspace generative AI, not Veo

The API OpenAPI schema at https://docs.dev.runwayml.com/openapi.json agrees: duration for model 'gen4.5' is 'an integer from 2 to 10'. Longer durations on Runway (e.g. Seedance 2.5 at 4-30s) belong to third-party models Runway hosts, not to Gen-4.5.
